definition_zh: 特许经营权；特许经营业务；选举权；特权；自由（古义）
definition_en: the right given by a company to sell its goods or use its name, or the business run under that right; also a formal privilege or the right to vote
core_image: 一把店门钥匙：品牌方把钥匙交给独立的经营者
scene: 街角新开了一家咖啡店，招牌是熟悉的连锁品牌，店主却不是总部的人。The local owner runs the coffee shop under a franchise from the brand.
sceneCN: 这里 franchise 是「特许经营授权」（第 4 个义项：在指定区域使用品牌经营的权利）；句意：这位本地店主凭品牌授予的特许经营权经营这家咖啡店。

pos.zh: 特许经营权；特许经营业务；选举权；特权
授予特许经营权；出售特许经营权

derivatives.zh: 由 franchise 加后缀 -ee 构成，指获得特许经营权的一方
由 franchise 加后缀 -or 构成，指授予特许经营权的一方
由 franchise 加 -ing 构成，指特许经营这种商业模式
en- 加 franchise，指给予选举权或使获得自由

senses.title: Freedom from servitude
senses.definition: the state of being free, especially freedom from a lord or from servitude
senses.definitionCN: 自由的状态，尤指不受领主控制或人身依附
senses.example: In medieval towns, franchise meant freedom from the control of a lord.
senses.exampleCN: 在中世纪的城镇里，这个词指不受领主控制的自由。
senses.why: Old French franchise simply meant freedom, the abstract state that the word first named.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 franchise 本义就是「自由」，这是该词最早命名的抽象状态。

senses.title: A granted privilege
senses.definition: a special right or exemption granted by a ruler or an authority
senses.definitionCN: 由统治者或权威机构授予的特殊权利或豁免
senses.example: The town received a franchise to hold a weekly market.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城镇获得了每周举办集市的特许权。
senses.why: A freedom becomes concrete when an authority grants it to a group, so franchise came to mean a charter of privileges.
senses.whyCN: 当权威机构把自由授予某个群体时，自由就具体化为特权，于是 franchise 有了「特许权」之义。

senses.title: The right to vote
senses.definition: the right of a citizen to vote in elections
senses.definitionCN: 公民在选举中投票的权利
senses.example: The nineteenth-century reforms widened the franchise.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪的改革扩大了选举权。
senses.why: A voting right is a privilege granted by law, the same shape as the older charter rights.
senses.whyCN: 选举权是法律授予的特权，与更早的特许权是同一种「被授予的权利」结构。

senses.title: A licensed brand right
senses.definition: an authorization to sell a company goods or services, or to use its name and methods, in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 在特定区域内销售某公司的商品或服务、使用其名称与经营方法的授权
senses.example: The bakery sold a franchise to a young couple in the next town.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店把特许经营权卖给了邻镇的一对年轻夫妇。
senses.why: Modern commerce turns the granted privilege into a licence for a brand, which is the dominant sense today.
senses.whyCN: 现代商业把「被授予的特权」变成了品牌授权，这是今天最主要的义项。

senses.title: The business so operated
senses.definition: the shop or company that operates under such an authorization
senses.definitionCN: 在这种授权下经营的店铺或公司
senses.example: She manages a franchise with twelve staff.
senses.exampleCN: 她经营着一家雇有十二名员工的特许经营店。
senses.why: The right and the business it creates are named by one word, a common shift from licence to outlet.
senses.whyCN: 权利与由它产生的生意共用一个词，这是从「许可」到「门店」的常见转义。

senses.title: To grant a franchise
senses.definition: to give a person or company the right to sell goods or use a name under agreed terms
senses.definitionCN: 按约定条款赋予个人或公司销售商品或使用品牌名称的权利
senses.example: The group franchises its gyms to local partners across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 该集团把健身房的特许经营权授予全国各地的本地合作伙伴。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: the brand owner now performs the act of granting the privilege.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的方向反过来：品牌方现在执行「授予特权」这个动作。

intro.en: Franchise comes from Old French franchise, freedom or exemption, from franc, free, a word tied to the Frankish ruling class.
intro.cn: franchise 来自古法语 franchise（自由、豁免），源于 franc（自由的），这个词与法兰克统治阶层有关。

items.en: Late Latin francus means free, a sense recorded in medieval documents.
items.cn: 一般认为晚期拉丁语 francus 意为「自由的」，这一含义见于中世纪文献。

items.en: Franc means free or noble, and franchise names the state of being free.
items.cn: franc 意为自由的、高贵的，franchise 指自由的状态。

items.en: Franchise enters English as a legal word for a privilege or an exemption.
items.cn: franchise 以法律用语的身份进入英语，指特权或豁免。

items.en: The word extends to the right to vote and to chartered privileges.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到选举权与特许权利。

items.en: American business gives franchise its commercial sense of a licensed brand right.
items.cn: 美国商业赋予 franchise 品牌授权的商业含义。

note.en: Franchise is the noun of a granted freedom, close to franchisee, franchisor, and to words for licences.
note.cn: franchise 是表示「被授予的自由」的名词，与 franchisee、franchisor 以及表示许可的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person or company that holds a franchise
entries.definitionCN: 持有特许经营权的人或公司
授予特许经营权的公司

entries.definition: the former currency of France and some other countries
entries.definitionCN: 法国等国的旧货币法郎；只是拼写相近，词源不同
授予权利的正式文件；特许状

entries.definition: a right granted by an authority to run a business
entries.definitionCN: 当局授予的经营权；特许权

normalIntro.en: Franchise is a freedom that someone grants, so the word covers voting rights as well as brand licences.
normalIntro.cn: franchise 是「别人授予的自由」，所以它既指选举权，也指品牌授权。

normal.en: The franc root means free, so franchise begins as freedom.
normal.cn: franc 词根意为自由，所以 franchise 最初就是自由。

normal.en: A town could buy a franchise, a bundle of chartered privileges.
normal.cn: 城镇可以买下 franchise，也就是一束特许权利。

normal.en: The franchise is also the vote, a right granted by law.
normal.cn: franchise 也指投票权，即法律授予的权利。

normal.en: In business a franchise is a licence to use a brand and its methods.
normal.cn: 在商业中，franchise 是使用品牌及其经营方法的许可。

normal.en: Keep franchise and franchisee apart: the first is the right, the second is the holder.
normal.cn: 要分清 franchise 与 franchisee：前者是权利，后者是持有者。

abstract.en: Picture an open gate where a lord once held the key.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇曾经由领主掌管钥匙的敞开大门。

abstract.en: Imagine a sealed scroll handed down from a ruler to a town.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷由统治者交给城镇的密封文书。

abstract.en: Think of a ballot box that only a few hands were once allowed to fill.
abstract.cn: 想象一个曾经只允许少数人投递的票箱。

examples.en: The chain granted her a franchise to open a store downtown.
examples.cn: 这家连锁店授予她在市中心开店的经营权。

examples.en: He bought a franchise of the coffee brand last spring.
examples.cn: 去年春天他买下了这个咖啡品牌的特许经营权。

examples.en: The new law gave the franchise to citizens over eighteen.
examples.cn: 新法律把选举权扩大到十八岁以上的公民。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗兰柴斯」——把自由「租」出去收租金，就是特许经营；只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 古法语 franc（自由的）→ franchise（自由、豁免）→ 英语 franchise（特权、选举权、特许经营权），核心义「被授予的自由」。

sensesIntro.en: Franchise runs from plain freedom, through a chartered privilege and the vote, to the commercial licence and the business it creates, and finally to the verb of granting.
sensesIntro.cn: franchise 从单纯的自由出发，经过特许权与选举权，走到商业授权及其产生的门店，最后作动词表示授予。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key to a shop door handed over by the brand owner.
core.cn: 核心意象：品牌方把店门钥匙交到经营者手里。

branches.en: Plain freedom is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 单纯的自由是最古老的义项。

branches.en: A granted privilege turns freedom into a charter.
branches.cn: 被授予的特权把自由变成一纸特许。

branches.en: The vote is a legal privilege in the same family.
branches.cn: 选举权是同一家族中的法律特权。

branches.en: Commercial licence and the outlet it creates share one word.
branches.cn: 商业授权与由此产生的门店共用一个词。

branches.en: The noun right and the verb of granting face each other.
branches.cn: 名词的「权利」与动词的「授予」彼此相对。

intro.en: Franchise is built on the Old French root franc, free, with English words for the holder, the giver, and the act of granting.
intro.cn: franchise 建立在古法语词根 franc（自由的）之上，英语围绕它构成持有人、授予方与授予行为等词。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin francus means free, and the Old French noun franchise carries that freedom into law.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 francus 意为自由的，古法语名词 franchise 把这份自由带进法律。

items.example: Franc is the root of franchise.
items.exampleCN: franc 是 franchise 的词根。

items.example: Old French franchise named a legal freedom.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 franchise 指法律上的自由。

items.meaning: a privilege or the right to vote
items.example: The English noun first meant a privilege.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语名词最初指特权。

items.meaning: a licence to use a brand
items.example: The business sense arose in the United States.
items.exampleCN: 商业义项兴起于美国。

items.example: The firm franchises its brand to partners.
items.exampleCN: 该公司把品牌授权给合作伙伴。
后缀 -ee 构成 franchisee。
franchisee 指接受授权的一方。
后缀 -or 构成 franchisor。
franchisor 指授予授权的公司。

items.example: Enfranchise adds the prefix en- to franchise.
items.exampleCN: enfranchise 在 franchise 前加了前缀 en-。

items.example: Franchising spread the brand across the country.
items.exampleCN: 特许经营把这个品牌推广到全国。

definition_zh: 供应商；供货方；供应者；（古）补足者
definition_en: a person or company that provides goods or services that others need
core_image: 一辆装满货箱的卡车停在仓库门口，把空掉的货架补满
scene: 仓库的货架空了，一辆卡车停在门口，司机把装箱单递给采购员。The driver works for a supplier of machine parts.
sceneCN: 这里 supplier 是「供应商」（第 1 个义项：向其他企业提供货物的公司）；句意：这位司机为一家机器零件供应商工作。

derivatives.zh: 供应；提供（supplier 的基础动词与名词）
供应品；补给（supply 的复数名词）
供应；供货（动词 supply 的动名词）

senses.title: A company that provides goods
senses.definition: a company that sells goods to another company or shop
senses.definitionCN: 向另一家公司或商店出售货物的公司
senses.example: The factory ordered parts from three suppliers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂向三家供应商订购了零件。
senses.why: Supplier is the agent noun of supply, so the core image is one who fills what another lacks.
senses.whyCN: supplier 是 supply 的施动名词，核心意象就是「把别人缺的东西补齐的人」。

senses.title: A provider of a service or resource
senses.definition: a person or organization that provides a service, energy, or water to users
senses.definitionCN: 向用户提供服务、能源或水的个人或组织
senses.example: The energy supplier cut off the gas to the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 这家能源供应商切断了整条街的燃气。
senses.why: The agent noun extends from goods to any continuous resource that is delivered.
senses.whyCN: 这个施动名词从货物扩展到任何持续输送的资源。

senses.title: The party that supplies under a contract
senses.definition: the party in a commercial contract who must provide the goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 商业合同中必须提供货物或服务的一方
senses.example: If the supplier delivers late, the buyer may claim damages.
senses.exampleCN: 如果供货方延迟交货，买方可以要求赔偿损失。
senses.why: Contract law fixes the general provider into a named role with duties.
senses.whyCN: 合同法把一般的供应者固定成一个有明确义务的角色。

senses.title: A person who provides something needed
senses.definition: a person who gives or provides something that others need
senses.definitionCN: 向他人提供所需之物的个人
senses.example: Her uncle was a supplier of books to the village school.
senses.exampleCN: 她的叔叔曾是村里学校的图书供应者。
senses.why: Behind the company sense stands the simple human act of handing over what is needed.
senses.whyCN: 在公司义项背后，是「把需要的东西交出去」这一简单的人类行为。

senses.title: One who fills a lack
senses.definition: an old sense: one who fills up or completes what is missing
senses.definitionCN: 古义：把缺少的东西填满或补全的人
senses.example: In older texts a supplier was one who filled a vacancy.
senses.exampleCN: 在更早的文本里，supplier 指填补空缺的人。
senses.why: The Latin source supplere means to fill up, and the oldest agent sense keeps that image of completing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源 supplere 意为填满，最早的施动义保留了「补全」的意象。

intro.en: Supplier comes from supply, from Old French souploier, to fill up, from Latin supplere, to complete.
intro.cn: supplier 来自 supply，源于古法语 souploier（填满），再往前是拉丁语 supplere（补足）。

items.en: Supplere means to fill up or make complete.
It joins sub, from below, and plere, to fill.
items.cn: 它由 sub（从下）与 plere（填满）组合而成。

items.en: Souploier carries the sense of filling a need.
items.cn: souploier 承袭了「满足需要、补足」的含义。

items.en: Supply enters English as a verb meaning to fill or provide.
items.cn: supply 以动词身份进入英语，意为填补或提供。

items.en: The agent noun supplier names the one who provides.
items.cn: 施动名词 supplier 指提供货物的一方。

items.en: Supplier becomes a standard word for business vendors.
items.cn: supplier 成为商业中对供货方的标准称呼。

note.en: Supplier is the agent noun of supply, close to the verb, its forms, and to words for sellers.
note.cn: supplier 是 supply 的施动名词，与动词本身、其变形以及表示售卖者的词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 出售货物的公司；供应商

entries.definition: a person or company that provides a service
entries.definitionCN: 提供服务或资源的个人或公司

entries.definition: a person who buys and sells goods

normalIntro.en: Supplier is supply plus the agent ending, the one who fills an order.
normalIntro.cn: supplier 是 supply 加上表示施动者的词尾，指把订单补齐的一方。

normal.en: Supply comes from a Latin verb meaning to fill up.
normal.cn: supply 来自意为「填满」的拉丁语动词。

normal.en: A supplier fills the gap in another company stock.
normal.cn: 供应商填补另一家公司库存的空缺。

normal.en: The ending -ier marks the person or firm that does the supplying.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ier 标记执行供应的人或公司。

normal.en: An energy supplier delivers gas or power to homes.
normal.cn: 能源供应商向家庭输送燃气或电力。

normal.en: In a contract the supplier is the party who must deliver.
normal.cn: 在合同里，supplier 是必须交货的一方。

abstract.en: Picture a truck loading boxes into an empty warehouse.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆卡车把箱子装进空仓库。

abstract.en: Imagine a pipe that carries water into every kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象一根把水送进每家厨房的管道。

abstract.en: Think of a signed page where one party promises to deliver.
abstract.cn: 想象一页签好的文件，其中一方承诺交货。

examples.en: The bakery buys its flour from a local supplier.
examples.cn: 这家面包店从本地供应商那里购买面粉。

examples.en: Our supplier failed to deliver the order on time.
examples.cn: 我们的供应商未能按时交付订单。

examples.en: The hospital chose a new supplier of medical gloves.
examples.cn: 医院选定了新的医用手套供应商。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「苏普莱尔」——supply（供应）加上「人」，就是供货的人；只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（从下往上）+ plere（填满）→ supplere（补足）→ 古法语 souploier → 英语 supply → supplier（供应者），核心义「把缺的东西补齐」。

sensesIntro.en: Supplier starts as the agent noun of supply, naming the firm that provides goods, then any provider of a resource, then the contract party, and finally the older filler of a lack.
sensesIntro.cn: supplier 先是 supply 的施动名词，指向企业提供货物，再指资源供应方、合同供货方，最后保留「补足者」的古义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a truck filling the empty shelves of a warehouse.
core.cn: 核心意象：卡车把空货架重新填满。

branches.en: The goods supplier is the everyday business sense.
branches.cn: 货物供应商是最日常的商业义项。

branches.en: A resource provider extends the filling image to services.
branches.cn: 资源供应方把「填满」的意象扩展到服务。

branches.en: The contract party turns the provider into a legal role.
branches.cn: 合同供货方把供应者变成法律角色。

branches.en: Both goods and services are delivered to fill a need.
branches.cn: 货物与服务都是为填补需要而交付的。

branches.en: The provider, the contract party, and the old filler all complete a gap.
branches.cn: 供应者、合同供货方与古老义项中的补足者，都在补上一个缺口。

intro.en: Supplier grows from the Latin verb supplere, to fill up, through English supply and the agent suffix -ier.
intro.cn: supplier 从拉丁语动词 supplere（补足）经英语 supply 与施动词尾 -ier 发展而来。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplere means to fill up, built from sub, below, and plere, to fill.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 supplere 意为填满，由 sub（在下）与 plere（填满）构成。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 开启 supplere 一词。
plere 提供「填满」的意象。

items.example: Supplere is the direct source of supply.
items.exampleCN: supplere 是 supply 的直接来源。

items.example: Supply is the base of supplier.
items.exampleCN: supply 是 supplier 的基础词。
词尾 -ier 构成 supplier。
supplier 指提供货物的公司。
supplies 指备好的供应品。
供货让货架保持充足。
supplement 共享「填满」词根。

items.example: Supplementum is the Latin noun of supplere.
items.exampleCN: supplementum 是 supplere 的拉丁名词。

definition_zh: 补贴；补助金；（历史）议会拨给王室的款项；后备援助
definition_en: money paid by a government or authority to support an industry, keep prices low, or help a person or group
core_image: 后方粮车上备好的粮袋，前线缺粮时立刻推上前去
scene: 麦收前价格下跌，政府给种植小麦的农户发了一笔钱，让他们不至于亏本。The government paid a subsidy to wheat farmers to keep prices stable.
sceneCN: 这里 subsidy 是「政府补贴」（第 1 个义项：政府为支持生产或稳定价格而支付的款项）；句意：政府向麦农发放补贴以稳定价格。

derivatives.zh: 由 subsidy 加后缀 -ize 构成，指给予补贴、资助
由 subsidize 加 -ed 构成，指受补贴的
由 subsidize 加 -ation 构成，指补贴行为
同源于拉丁语 subsidiarius，指辅助的、次要的；作名词指子公司

senses.title: Government support for an industry
senses.definition: money a government pays to producers or sellers to lower prices or protect an industry
senses.definitionCN: 政府支付给生产者或销售者、用以降低价格或保护产业的款项
senses.example: The government offered a subsidy to keep bread prices low.
senses.exampleCN: 政府提供补贴以压低面包价格。
senses.why: The Latin source names troops held in reserve, money set behind the line to be used when needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源指留在后方的后备队，即备在战线之后、需要时动用的钱。

senses.title: A grant to a person or body
senses.definition: a sum granted to a person, family, or institution to help with costs
senses.definitionCN: 给予个人、家庭或机构以帮助支付费用的款项
senses.example: The charity received a subsidy for its housing project.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构为其住房项目获得了一笔补助金。
senses.why: From public money for industry the word extends to any grant that covers a gap.
senses.whyCN: 从支持产业的公共资金，这个词扩展到任何填补缺口的补助。

senses.title: A parliamentary grant to the Crown
senses.definition: a sum voted by Parliament to the sovereign for public purposes
senses.definitionCN: 议会为公共用途拨给君主的款项
senses.example: In the seventeenth century Parliament voted a subsidy to the king.
senses.exampleCN: 十七世纪时，议会投票通过拨给国王一笔款项。
senses.why: English history gave subsidy a precise legal sense: money voted to the Crown.
senses.whyCN: 英国历史赋予 subsidy 一个精确的法律含义：议会拨给王室的款项。

senses.title: Money for allied troops
senses.definition: money paid to an ally to hire soldiers or support a war
senses.definitionCN: 支付给盟国以雇用士兵或支持战争的款项
senses.example: The treaty promised a subsidy for the allied army.
senses.exampleCN: 条约承诺为盟军提供一笔款项。
senses.why: The oldest military sense survives: reserve troops paid from a supporting fund.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的军事义项仍在：由支援款项支付的后备军队。

senses.title: Help or support in general
senses.definition: support or aid given to a person or cause
senses.definitionCN: 给予个人或事业的援助与支持
senses.example: The plan relies on a subsidy from private donors.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划依靠私人捐助者的资助。
senses.why: The monetary sense lightens into general help, keeping the idea of support from behind.
senses.whyCN: 金钱义淡化了一般的帮助，但仍保留「从后方支援」的意思。

intro.en: Subsidy comes from Latin subsidium, reserve troops or help, from sub, behind, and sedere, to sit.
intro.cn: subsidy 来自拉丁语 subsidium（后备队、援助），由 sub（在后）与 sedere（坐）构成。

items.en: Subsidium first names troops kept in reserve behind the line.
items.cn: subsidium 最初指留在战线后方的后备队。

items.en: It is built from sub, behind, and sedere, to sit.
items.cn: 它由 sub（在后）与 sedere（坐）构成。

items.en: Subside carries the sense of help or support into French.
items.cn: subside 把「援助、支持」的含义带入法语。

items.en: Subsidy enters English as money granted by Parliament.
items.cn: subsidy 以「议会拨付的款项」进入英语。

items.en: Modern use adds state aid to industry and to households.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了国家对产业与家庭的援助。

note.en: Subsidy is the noun of money held in reserve, close to its verb family and to words for grants.
note.cn: subsidy 是表示「留作后备的钱」的名词，与它的动词词族以及表示补助的词相邻。

entries.definition: auxiliary or secondary; a branch company
money given for a particular purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途提供的款项；拨款

entries.definition: a regular sum paid to help with costs
entries.definitionCN: 为帮助支付费用而定期给予的款项

entries.definition: help or support given to a person or country
entries.definitionCN: 给予个人或国家的援助

normalIntro.en: Subsidy is money kept behind the line, ready to support whatever is short in front.
normalIntro.cn: subsidy 是备在战线后方的钱，随时支援前方短缺之处。

normal.en: The Latin root is reserve troops, money waiting behind the front.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根是后备队，即在前线后方待命的钱。

normal.en: A subsidy is paid by a government, not earned in a sale.
normal.cn: subsidy 由政府支付，而不是在交易中赚得。

normal.en: Farm subsidies keep food prices from falling too low.
normal.cn: 农业补贴防止食品价格跌得过低。

normal.en: The verb is subsidize: to pay such a grant.
normal.cn: 动词是 subsidize，意为支付这类补贴。

normal.en: Keep subsidy and subsidiary apart: the first is the money, the second is a branch company.
normal.cn: 要分清 subsidy 与 subsidiary：前者是钱，后者是子公司。

abstract.en: Picture a grain cart kept behind the front line.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆停在前线后方的粮车。

abstract.en: Imagine a sealed envelope with money for a family in need.
abstract.cn: 想象一个装着钱、寄给困难家庭的密封信封。

abstract.en: Think of a chest of coins voted to the king in Parliament.
abstract.cn: 想象一箱在议会投票通过后拨给国王的钱币。

examples.en: The government cut the subsidy on fossil fuels last year.
examples.cn: 政府去年削减了化石燃料补贴。

examples.en: Farmers depend on a subsidy to survive a bad harvest.
examples.cn: 农民依靠补贴度过歉收。

examples.en: The city offers a subsidy for new solar panels.
examples.cn: 这座城市为新太阳能板提供补贴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨布赛迪」——听上去像「撒补贴」，政府往你兜里撒钱；只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在后）+ sedere（坐）→ subsidium（坐在后方的后备队、援助）→ 英语 subsidy（援助→议会拨款→政府补贴），核心义「留在后方、随时补上的支援」。

sensesIntro.en: Subsidy begins as reserve troops, becomes a grant of money voted by Parliament, then state aid to industry, then any grant or general support.
sensesIntro.cn: subsidy 从后备军队起步，变为议会拨付的款项，再指国家对产业的补贴，最后泛指补助与支持。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grain cart waiting behind the front line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆停在前线后方待命的粮车。

branches.en: State aid to producers is the central modern sense.
branches.cn: 国家对生产者的补贴是核心的现代义项。

branches.en: A grant to a person or body widens the same money idea.
branches.cn: 给个人或机构的补助金拓宽了同一种金钱观念。

branches.en: The parliamentary grant is the precise historical sense.
branches.cn: 议会拨款是精确的历史义项。

branches.en: Money for allied troops keeps the oldest military image.
branches.cn: 雇用盟军的款项保留了最古老的军事意象。

branches.en: Subsidy, grant, and support all answer a shortage from behind.
branches.cn: 补贴、补助与支持，都是从后方回应短缺。

intro.en: Subsidy is built on the Latin noun subsidium, with English words for paying, receiving, and the act of support.
intro.cn: subsidy 建立在拉丁语名词 subsidium 之上，英语围绕它构成支付、受助与支援行为等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin subsidium means reserve troops or help, from sub, behind, and sedere, to sit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 subsidium 意为后备队或援助，来自 sub（在后）与 sedere（坐）。

items.example: The prefix sub- places the troops behind.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把军队安置在后。

items.example: Sedere gives the image of sitting in reserve.
items.exampleCN: sedere 提供「坐守后备」的意象。
subsidium 是直接来源。

items.example: Subsidy keeps the modern money sense.
items.exampleCN: subsidy 保留现代的金钱义项。

items.example: Subsidize turns the noun into an action.
items.exampleCN: subsidize 把名词变成动作。

items.example: Subsidized describes a supported buyer or seller.
items.exampleCN: subsidized 描述受到补贴的买方或卖方。
后缀 -ize 构成 subsidize。
subsidization 指补贴这一政策行为。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 构成 subsidization。
subsidiary 保留「后备」的含义。
subsidiarius 是拉丁形容词。
